result_text:
**I can't give you a single answer. The evidence plus your own ranges don't settle ship versus hold, so the call goes back to the release owner.** The verdict is `prior-sensitive`, and it is also loss-sensitive.

The full record is at `work/decision-record.md`.

**The update**
- The only usable evidence is that the canary/control gap was above 40 ms (57 ms observed).
- In your reference class of 20 past rollouts, the gap appeared in 9 of 10 real regressions and 2 of 10 non-regressions. That gives a likelihood ratio of 4.5.
- I did not use the 10/10 split as a base rate, because the ledger says those strata were quota-drawn.
- Neither UNRESOLVED status counts as evidence by itself.
- Your prior odds of 0.02–0.2 (1:50 to 1:5) become posterior odds of 0.09–0.9.

**The decision rule**
- Hold if prior odds × 4.5 × loss ratio L > 1, which simplifies to prior odds × L > 0.222.
- The cost of a miss relative to a needless hold is L, in your range of 2 to 20.

**Where the answer flips**

| Loss ratio L | Prior odds at which ship becomes the better call |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | below 0.111 (1:9) |
| 5 | below 0.044 |
| 10 | below 0.022 |
| 11.1 or more | never within your prior range, so hold |
| 20 | below 0.0111, outside your range, so hold |

- If your prior is 1:5, hold wins at every loss ratio you gave.
- If your prior is 1:50, ship wins unless the miss cost is above about 11 times a hold.
- Ship wins only in the low-prior, low-loss corner, roughly 28% of the log-scaled grid. That figure describes the sweep, not a belief.

**How fragile the likelihood ratio is.** With only 10 rollouts per stratum, a conservative range for the ratio is about 1.2–17 (Wilson 95% intervals). At the low end, ship wins over much more of the grid. At the high end, hold wins almost everywhere.

**What would move it**
- The decisive input is T2, the raw access-log p95 on the canary hosts. It is the only test that separates a real regression from an exporter artifact. The restore request was still pending when the ledger closed on 2026-09-10.
- If T2 can run before the freeze, it would move the decision far more than any prior or loss number you could agree on. A hold costs one unit, so waiting on it is cheap.
- Pricing that restore properly would need a separate value-of-information record, which I haven't done.
- If T2 can't run in time, the loss ratio and prior are what's left to argue about. Hold is the safer default unless the team believes both the prior is below about 1:9 and a miss costs only about 2 times a hold.

**Assumptions to check**
- The release owner isn't named in the request or ledger.
- The ledger doesn't say what undoing a shipped regression costs. I treated that as folded into L.
- The ratio assumes this rollout resembles the 20 past ones.
- The past gaps came from the same metrics pipeline that H2 questions.
- The ledger is as of 2026-09-10 and I haven't seen anything newer.

This is a recommendation framework only. It doesn't authorize shipping, holding, or pulling the logs.
